messages:
Alana: Observed gradual KV cache memory growth on Dedicated over 48h for long-context flows (ctx ~65k). Hosted runs same workload but does not show the same steady increase. Posting profiling snippets and notes.
Devon: interesting — is this the same canary workload? any kernel / cgroup diffs between the envs?
Alana: Canary and prod runs use the same model and request shapes. Key differences: Dedicated nodes are on-prem A100 with NVLink (kernel 6.1), Hosted runs on GCE (kernel 5.4) under cgroups v2. Notable tunables: Dedicated vm.swappiness=30, Hosted vm.swappiness=10; Hosted also has cgroup memory.high configured.
Mike: Could memory.high on Hosted force earlier reclaim and keep resident KV smaller? That would explain the divergence.
Alana: Profiling supports that — Hosted shows earlier page reclaim activity (anon reclaim / kcompact spikes), Dedicated delays reclaim until working set grows causing slab fragmentation and slow backfills.
SRE-Bot: deploy-alert: repro-run to dedicated-cluster completed (rc=0)
Kevin: We've seen allocator behavior flip when pages are scarce vs when cgroups bound. Kernel selection impacts madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) semantics, hugepage demotion, and whether async reclaim is used.
Ingrid: Can you paste the minimal repro commands / perf captures we should run on Dedicated? I can schedule a repro node.
Alana: Short snippet from the Dedicated node during the long-ctx run:
```
# on dedicated node during steady growth window
cat /proc/vmstat | egrep 'pgpgin|pgpgout|pswpin|pswpout'
pgpgin 123456
pgpgout 78901
pswpin 0
pswpout 0
```
Also saw increasing "pgsteal" events in perf, and slab fragmentation rising in /sys/kernel/slab/*/active_objs.
Devon: pswp* = 0 means no swap used, but lots of pgpgin/out implies pagecache churn. That pattern can leave KV pages resident but scattered across frames -> higher fragmentation and worse allocator compactions.
Mike: Actionable experiments: (A) lower vm.swappiness on Dedicated to 10; (B) enable cgroup memory.high for the KV service to force earlier reclaim; (C) toggle transparent hugepages to observe slab coalescing effects.
Alana: Another config mismatch: vm.max_map_count differed (hosted=262144, dedicated=65536). Low map counts on Dedicated cause more allocation failures and fallback code paths that increase fragmentation.
Kevin: Also note batching heuristic change last week: dedicated-config unintentionally increased max_batch_time from 5ms -> 12ms. Longer batching windows increase per-request live KV lifetime, which could amplify growth.
Ingrid: I'll spin a small repro cluster on Dedicated with adjustable tunables. Would like to collect: perf record -e page-faults, a flamegraph of kv allocator, /proc/vmstat, and slab active counts over time.
Alana: I'll pair with you. I'll also attach the batching config we used. Summary of immediate plan: (1) repro with vm.swappiness=10 + mem.high enabled; (2) repro with vm.max_map_count bumped to hosted levels; (3) collect perf + slab counters; (4) test reducing max_batch_time back to 5ms to measure impact.
Devon: If repro shows earlier reclaim reduces steady-state KV footprint, we should consider a conservative default config for Dedicated (mem.high + lower swappiness) and document for Private/on-prem.
Mike: Also worth testing kernel 6.1 on Hosted or backport patches that change madvise/hugepage demotion behavior to see if kernel fixes help.
SRE-Bot: note: assigned Ingrid + Alana to this repro task
Alana: Thanks — will update thread with captures and a short action PR. :mag:
